review_notes: Reviewed all 81 lines of the target and the related model, affine-limit, and rank-one norm definitions. The proposed closed-unit-ball version uses the same limit argument after establishing that 1 − outerSym w is positive semidefinite when ‖w‖ ≤ 1; the rank-one norm limit then contributes the factor ‖u‖². No other justified specialization was identified.

findings.excerpt:
(u v : Vec 4) (hu : ‖u‖ = 1) (hv : ‖v‖ = 1) (y : Fin 3 → ℝ) :
    choiLam (wedgeCoordinates v u) y =
      operatorNorm (P.leftProjection v * P.B y * P.rightProjection u) ^ 2
findings.problem: The unit-vector assumptions can be weakened to closed-unit-ball assumptions, which include zero and non-unit vectors for which the affine path remains positive. With general u in that ball, the rank-one limit has norm ‖outer u‖ = ‖u‖², so the displayed identity needs that factor.
findings.proposed_change: Use `(hu : ‖u‖ ≤ 1) (hv : ‖v‖ ≤ 1)` and state `choiLam (wedgeCoordinates v u) y * ‖u‖ ^ 2 = operatorNorm (P.leftProjection v * P.B y * P.rightProjection u) ^ 2`. Establish positivity of `1 - outerSym w` from ‖w‖ ≤ 1 (by the inner-product Cauchy–Schwarz bound), then use the existing affine positive-definiteness and inverse-square-root limit arguments. In the rank-one norm step, replace the unit-vector norm simplification with the general rank-one norm `‖outer u‖ = ‖u‖²`.
findings.benefit: The identity would apply to vectors throughout the closed unit ball, including the degenerate zero-vector cases, while retaining the unit-vector result as a special case. The projection definitions already accept arbitrary vectors.

evidence.excerpt:
have hH (w : Vec 4) (hw : ‖w‖ = 1) :
      ((1 - outerSym w : Sym 4) : Mat 4 ℝ).PosSemidef :=
    one_sub_outer_posSemidef w hw

(hH : (H : Mat n ℝ).PosSemidef) :
    Tendsto (fun t : ℝ => inverseSquareRoot (1 + (t - 1) • H)) atTop

def NormalizedPencil.leftProjection (P : NormalizedPencil) (v : Vec 4) : Mat P.a ℝ :=
  kernelProjection (P.D (1 - outerSym v) : Mat P.a ℝ)
